chunks: Everything in this book that is from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, I have narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār, may Allah be pleased with him, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb together, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj al-Bajalī al-Kūfī.

He was a mawlā, and he had met al-Ṣādiq and Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام and narrated from them both. Mūsā عليه السلام, when he was mentioned in his presence, would say: “Indeed, he is weighty in the heart.”

key_terms.لَثَقِيلٌ فِي الْفُؤَادِ: A phrase indicating weight, gravity, and strong impression in the heart.
key_terms.مَوْلًى: A freedman or client affiliated with a tribe.
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَ: Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام, named here with Imam al-Ṣādiq عليهما السلام.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain and biographical status of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage gives the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, then briefly identifies him biographically. It notes that he met Imam al-Ṣādiq and Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام and preserves a statement from Imam Mūsā عليه السلام indicating his grave standing and significance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abdur Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj has been transmitted by me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Attar - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub together, from Abdur Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj Al-Bajali Al-Kufi.

He was a freed servant (mawla) who met Imam Al-Sadiq and Imam Musa ibn Jafar (peace be upon them) and narrated from both of them. Imam Musa (as), when Abdur Rahman was mentioned in his presence, would say: "Indeed, he weighs heavily on the heart."
